meanings: verb: to publicly agree with and support
examples: The teacher's union endorsed the candidate's plan to increase school funding by placing a higher tax on cigarettes.

meanings: verb: to continue to exist, staying important or common
examples: Despite the best efforts of environmentalists around the world, oil, gas, and coal have prevailed as the main sources of energy.

meanings: verb: to take control of power or energy in order to use it
examples: "If you could just harness some of that youthful energy," said my mother, "you'd be able to get better grades."

meanings: adjective: a little bit chaotic or violent and disorganized
examples: The once calm classroom grew turbulent when a hand-sized spider ran across the floor.

meanings: adjective: with uneven edges; torn
examples: I tried to sell my textbooks after I graduated, but their pages were so ragged that nobody would buy them.

meanings: verb: to mention a topic in order to make people feel a certain way
examples: The strongest argument to preserve the land as a national park came from the local natives, who invoked the respect for nature of their ancestors.

meanings: noun: a situation that seems impossible because it is made of opposite things
examples: When he first arrived in the desert, Alex did not believe the paradox that drinking hot tea could make a person feel cool.

meanings: adjective: quick and energetic
examples: Alice walked at such a brisk pace that Frank began sweating trying to stay next to her.

meanings: verb: to say officially that a normal requirement isn't required
examples: The government decided to waive the minimum number of classes needed to maintain student visas for those who met family requirements instead.

meanings: adjective: unchanging and stubborn
examples: Starting a career as a poet is almost impossible today—only the most tenacious writers follow their dreams long enough to find success.

meanings: adjective: possible to do without problem
examples: Our global economy is so complicated that it is not feasible for one person to understand it entirely.

meanings: noun: fear that something bad will happen
examples: Every time I get on an airplane, I breathe deeply and tell myself it's safe, but still I have a feeling of apprehension as we take off.

meanings: adjective: not used anymore
examples: Vinyl records are generally obsolete as a way to play music, but some collectors value them highly for their distinctive sound.

meanings: adjective: impossible to reversed
examples: Fleeing his country was Abraham's best chance at survival, but once he left his decision would be irrevocable.

meanings: adjective: describing a statement that is not believable
examples: Sally knew James was lying because his story was so implausible—nobody could have stayed awake for 80 straight hours.

meanings: adjective: extremely large
examples: Few appreciate the colossal size of the sun: if hollow, it could contain a million Earths.

meanings: adjective: more than is needed, desired, or required
examples: The dictionary has provided all of its content online for free, so buying the book is superfluous for anyone with a smartphone.

meanings: adjective: with a very strong effect
examples: A cup of tea can be nice, but when you need to stay awake, espresso is a more potent solution.

meanings: adjective: small, warm, and comfortable
examples: After hiking for hours through the snow, Janice felt warm and cozy resting under a thick blanket with a cup of hot cocoa.

meanings: adjective: inactive now but able to become active later
examples: A wasp in winter may seem to be frozen when in fact she is merely hibernating; she is not dead, but dormant.

meanings: verb: to cause feelings or responses to come out
examples: Just smiling—even if you are depressed—can elicit feelings of pleasure and happiness.

meanings: adjective: without the possibility of success
examples: "I am far too powerful to be stopped now," boasted the evil wizard. "Your quest is futile."

meanings: adjective: exteremely important in order to succeed
examples: The CEO made it very clear to his employees that quick development and publication of results were pivotal to ensure more funding.

meanings: verb: to make small changes to improve
examples: The lawyer suggested amending the current contract rather than starting work on an entirely new deal.

meanings: adjective: extremely strongly felt
examples: Louise felt a profound dislike for the rude young man who spat on the street in front of her.

meanings: adjective: imitating or based on
examples: Most of the fashions this year are derivative; they copy the style that was popular a few years ago.

meanings: adjective: rough and uneven or rocky
examples: Mountain paths tend to be covered in tree roots and a mixture of rocks, making strong footwear important when dealing with the rugged ground.

meanings: adjective: possible to be done successfully
examples: The lost hikers' plan to build a shelter before dark seemed much less viable when the sky grew cloudy.

meanings: adjective: not able to produce plants (of land)
examples: Many Americans think of the Sonoran Desert as entirely barren, unaware of the diverse ecosystem that actually survives in that harsh environment.

meanings: verb: to place among or between other things
examples: The garden was a mess, with unwanted grass interspersed throughout the flowers.

meanings: noun: a small piece that is left when most is gone
examples: A crumb of cheese on the table was the only remnant of last night's celebratory dinner.

meanings: noun: how a person thinks about the world
examples: With her warm smile and ability to find the advantages of even the worst situations, Janet became known in the office for her positive outlook.

meanings: adjective: awkward and without skill
examples: John is not trying to be destructive but is merely clumsy; most of the items he has broken were not in his line of sight when he bumped into them.

adjective: interestingly new or different
examples: The scientist devoted her career to discovering novel uses for plastics that would otherwise be thrown away.

meanings: noun: a violent, sudden, and large change
examples: The earthquake raised miles of land several feet higher in a single, massive upheaval.

meanings: adjective: very light or small (of a feeling or sense)
examples: A gust of cool autumn wind blew through the window, and Sebastian felt a faint chill on the back of his neck.

meanings: verb: to think of or plan an idea or system
examples: Students in Mr. Needham's physics class had to devise a method for protecting an egg as it was dropped from the roof of the school.

meanings: noun: the quality of being clever and original
examples: Although Thomas Edison is often remembered for his inventions and ingenuity, it was his talent in business that truly made him great.

meanings: adjective: with no emotion or interest
examples: Mr. Thompson was so talented at teaching math that even normally apathetic students took interest.

meanings: noun: a large number of something
examples: When Andrew tipped over the tall black bookshelf, scores of books and magazines came crashing to the floor.

meanings: verb: to break (of something very hard)
examples: Under the enormous weight of a modern city building, stones without enough support will fracture, leading to collapse.

meanings: verb: to completely destroy
examples: I tried eradicating the mosquitos in my apartment with a rolled up newspaper, but there were too many of them.

meanings: verb: to turn away from a plan or standard
examples: The delicious smell of croissants filled the air, but Sasha knew that if she stepped into the bakery, she would surely deviate from her diet.

meanings: adjective: not enough in amount
examples: Aunt Lu's meager collection of board games was not enough to keep the children entertained on a rainy day.

meanings: verb: to combine two different things into one
examples: The scientist realized that it would be faster to buy the more complex chemicals instead of synthesizing them from simpler ones.

meanings: adjective: very noticeable and unusual
examples: Most of the people in the picture were smiling, but one little child looked out at the photographer with a striking frown.

meanings: noun: a comparison of two very different things that have one similar aspect
examples: There are surprising analogies we can make between medicine and warfare, especially in cancer treatment, which uses radiation to attack tumors.

meanings: adjective: perfectly calm
examples: Feeling entirely relaxed, Abigail looked at the ocean out her window with a serene smile on her face.

meanings: adjective: wealthy
examples: The homes at the top of the hill are so large and beautiful that only the highly affluent can afford them.

meanings: noun: an agreement reached by a whole group of people
examples: Alicia and her sisters argued for weeks about who would live in the house their parents had left, eventually reaching a consensus to simply sell it.
